title: What are you really selling?
principle: Sell what it means to them, not just what it is.

screens.text: Let me tell you about a washing powder. For years, washing powder ads in India promised clothes with no stains. Then in 2005, Surf Excel said something surprising: stains are good. "Daag acche hain."

screens.title: Stains are good
screens.text: In one ad, a little girl falls into a muddy puddle and cries. Her big brother jumps in and fights the puddle to protect her. He gets covered in mud. The message is simple: if you get dirty doing something good, those stains are good.

screens.prompt: Every powder said it removed stains. What do you think "stains are good" was really selling to parents?

options.label: Clothes that cost less to wash

screens.why: It sold the idea of being a parent who lets children play and stand up for others. Every powder removed stains. Surf showed what that meant for your child.

screens.title: Means–end laddering
screens.text: Marketers call this a means–end ladder. It has three steps. The bottom is a feature: what the product is or does. The middle is a benefit: what that lets you do. The top is a value: what it means to you.

screens.title: Surf's ladder
screens.text: Surf's ladder: it removes tough stains, the feature. So children can play freely, the benefit. So you're a parent who lets them do good, the value. Buyers compare features, but they choose values. And the top step only works if the bottom step is true.

screens.title: Now look at your business
screens.text: Washing powder and cakes are different, but your bakery has a ladder too. It's mid-December. Your butter videos helped you keep your regular buyers, but families who order only sometimes still compare your ₹850 cake with the chain shop's ₹700 cake.

screens.prompt: Here are three lines about your cake in the wrong order. Put them in order, from the bottom step to the top.
steps: Your child can eat it safely
A birthday made at home, with love
screens.why: Well done. Real butter is what it is. Your child eating it safely is what that lets you do. A birthday made with love is what it means. Families choose with the top step, but it must be supported by a true fact.

screens.prompt: Which line should go on your cake boxes?

options.label: "Real butter, no preservatives, eggless, fresh daily"
"Real butter, no preservatives: made like home"
"Made with love, like a cake from home"

screens.why: Yes. The fact makes the feeling believable. The feeling shows why the fact matters. That's the whole ladder in one line.

wrong.a: All true, but these are only facts. Buyers compare facts and prices. The chain says "butter" too. Show what the facts mean: "Real butter, no preservatives: made like home."
wrong.c: A feeling without a fact is hard to believe. Any shop can say it. Join the feeling with a true fact: "Real butter, no preservatives: made like home."

screens.prompt: A chain shop says, "Baked with a mother's love." Its cakes are made in a factory with preservatives. What's wrong?

options.label: Nothing, many shops say things like this
The shop should show its low price
The cake does not support the claim

screens.why: Yes. A feeling without a true fact to support it is hard to believe. When buyers notice this, they stop trusting the shop.

wrong.a: Many ads say things like this. That's why buyers stop believing them. A feeling needs a true fact to support it. A factory cake with preservatives cannot support "a mother's love".
wrong.b: Price is another fact that rivals can beat. The real problem is that a factory cake with preservatives cannot support the feeling of "a mother's love".

screens.prompt: I'll show you six lines about a cake. For each one, tell me: does it say what it is or does, or what it means?

items.text: A birthday your child will remember
Your child's happiest day of the year
Share happy moments with people you love

screens.why: Butter, eggless and no preservatives tell you what the cake is. A birthday to remember, a happy day and time together tell you what it means. The best line joins a fact with a feeling.

screens.setup: It's mid-December. New Year parties are coming. The chain shop sells cakes for ₹700. Yours cost ₹850 and leave you ₹450 per cake. Your next post will reach 500 past buyers.
screens.question: What does it say?

options.label: "Real butter, eggless, no preservatives. ₹850."
options.outcome: Families agree your cake is good, but compare ₹850 with ₹700. 12 order, leaving you ₹5,400.
options.why: The facts are true, but they only show the bottom step. Buyers compare facts and prices.
options.better: Show what the facts mean: "Real butter, baked this morning: New Year at home."

options.label: "₹100 off this week only, real butter cakes!"
options.outcome: 14 order at ₹750, leaving you ₹350 per cake: ₹4,900. In January, families wait for your next offer.
options.why: You made buyers think about price. The chain shop already has a lower price.
options.better: Show what the facts mean: "Real butter, baked this morning: New Year at home."

options.label: "Real butter, baked this morning: New Year at home"
options.outcome: Families reply with photos of last year's party at home. 20 order at ₹850, leaving you ₹9,000. Nobody asks about the chain shop's price.
options.why: A true fact supported something families care about. They chose what the cake meant to them, not the cheaper cake.

screens.title: The honest line
screens.text: The line again: use on others only what you'd accept being used on you. Every step of the ladder must be true. A feeling your product cannot support, like "a mother's love" on a factory cake, is a trick, and buyers may notice.
Sell what it ___ to them, not just what it ___.
screens.why: Yes. Surf sold the idea of children who stand up for others, more than clean clothes. You sell a party that feels like home, supported by real butter.

summary: A means–end ladder: feature (what it is or does) → benefit (what that lets you do) → value (what it means).
Buyers compare features but choose values. Show both in one line.
Every step must be true. A feeling without a true fact is a trick.

cards.front: Which sells more: "99.7% pure ghee" or "99.7% pure, for your family's rotis"?
cards.back: Join a true fact with what it means to buyers. People choose what matters to them, not just what the product is.

cards.front: "Removes tough stains" is which step of the ladder?
cards.back: Feature: what it is or does. Benefit: what that lets you do. Value: what it means.

cards.front: A factory cake says "made with a mother's love". What's wrong?
options: No true fact supports the feeling
cards.back: Every step of the ladder must be true.

sources.label: Surf Excel's Daag Acche Hai campaign (Social Samosa, 2018)
